terminal.description: A terminal in your workspace. `node where.js` runs your script from here; `cd water` and then `node ../where.js` runs the same script from the water folder, and `cd ..` comes back.

tasks.title: Show both folders
tasks.description:
Write `where.js` so that it prints two lines:

```
Run from: <the folder the command was typed in>
Script in: <the folder that holds where.js>
```

Each is a full path. From the top folder of the workspace they are the same; from the `water` folder, with `node ../where.js`, they differ.

Check runs `where.js` from the top folder and from `water`, and compares each line with the real folder.
nextSteps: Print the folder the command was typed in: `process` knows it.
Print the folder of the script: a module knows its own.
Run `node where.js` from the top folder.
Run `cd water`, then `node ../where.js`, and see the first line change.
hints: The folder the command was typed in is the working directory. A module's own place is on `import.meta`.
`process.cwd()` gives the working directory. `import.meta.dirname` gives the folder that holds the module.

tasks.title: Add up the water from any folder
tasks.description:
Each line of `water/readings.txt` is a date, a trough and the litres used: `2026-06-01,north,420`. Write `water-total.js` so that it prints the litres of all the lines added up:

```
Total: 2622 litres
```

It reads `water/readings.txt` beside the script, whatever folder the command is typed in, so `node ../water-total.js` from the `water` folder works too. Build the path with `join` from `node:path`, never by putting text and slashes together.

Check writes readings of its own into `water/readings.txt`, runs `water-total.js` from three folders, and reads how the path is built.
nextSteps: Build the path to the readings from the script's own folder.
Read the file and split it into lines, leaving out blank ones.
Add up the third part of every line as a number.
Run it from the top folder and from `water`: the total is the same.
hints: `'water/readings.txt'` on its own is looked for in the folder the command was typed in. From `water` that is `water/water/readings.txt`.
`join(import.meta.dirname, 'water', 'readings.txt')` is the readings file beside the script, with the right separator for the system.
`const text = await readFile(join(import.meta.dirname, 'water', 'readings.txt'), 'utf8')`, then sum `Number(line.split(',')[2])` over the lines.

tasks.title: Describe a path that was typed
tasks.description:
Write `file-info.js` so that `node file-info.js water/readings.txt` prints three lines about the path typed after the script's name:

```
Full path: <the full path, from the folder the command was typed in>
Name: readings.txt
Extension: .txt
```

A name with no dot has no extension: then the last line is `Extension: none`. The file does not have to exist. With no path at all, the script prints one line on standard error and ends with exit code 1. Take the parts with `node:path`, never by splitting at slashes.

Check runs `file-info.js` from three folders with paths of its own, written the way the system writes them, and with none.
nextSteps: Read the path typed after the script's name.
Turn it into a full path from the folder the command was typed in.
Take its name and its extension with functions of `node:path`.
Try it from the `water` folder with a path that starts with `..`.
hints: A path a person types is relative to where they typed it, not to the script. `node:path` has a function that turns it into a full path from there.
`resolve(typed)` starts from `process.cwd()`. `basename()` gives the last part of a path and `extname()` the end of it from the last dot.
